title: Privacy-classified TTL blueprints for prompts, responses, logs, and metrics
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Create a set of reusable TTL (time-to-live) blueprint templates that map privacy classifications (sensitivity tags) to retention behaviors across four artifact classes: prompts, model responses, request logs, and aggregated metrics. Blueprints will support inheritance, per-route overrides, sampled archival, and automated evidence exports to support audits.
background: Customers need fine-grained retention controls that reflect legal and product needs (e.g., user PII, anonymized telemetry, and ephemeral conversational histories). Existing per-route TTLs are ad-hoc and hard to reason about; audit evidence for deletions or sampled exports is manual and scattered. This initiative standardizes templates that non-legal engineers and security reviewers can apply consistently.
goals: Define privacy classification schema and default TTL mappings for prompts, responses, logs, and metrics
Ship TTL blueprint CRUD in Console + API and a CLI for bulk application
Allow per-route and per-tenant overrides with clear inheritance rules
Automate evidence export (signed bundle) whenever retention-triggered deletions or sampled archival occur
Provide retention impact simulator in Console to preview storage, cost, and audit artifacts
scope: TTL blueprint model and API (CRUD + apply/unapply)
Console UX to author and assign blueprints to routes/tenants
Automated evidence bundle generation for retention actions (signed manifest, count, checksums)
Retention simulator that estimates token counts, storage, and sample sizes
Migration tool to suggest blueprint mappings from existing adhoc TTLs
out_of_scope: New data residency (region) enforcement — handled by separate project
Long-term cold archival pipeline changes beyond export format
Changes to runtime encryption/KMS integrations (coordination only)
success_metrics: >80% of new routes assigned a TTL blueprint within 30 days of launch
Reduce manual evidence export tickets by 90% for retention incidents
Console retention simulator accuracy within ±10% of actual storage costs for 90% of tested routes
No customer-facing incidents caused by automated retention deletions in the first quarter post-launch
acceptance_criteria: Admin can create/edit/delete TTL blueprints with a privacy classification and per-artifact TTLs
API endpoints to list and apply blueprints to a route or tenant exist and are documented
Inheritance semantics documented: global -> tenant -> route -> route-override, with explicit precedence
Automated evidence bundle created and stored in S3 (signed manifest + checksum + deletion log) for every retention-triggered purge
Retention simulator available in Console that accepts route throughput and returns estimated storage and sample volumes
E2E tests that simulate a deletion window and validate evidence bundle contents and signatures
Design reviewed and approved by Design (see design link) and documented in Confluence
risk_mitigation: Retention actions will run in staging first and produce evidence bundles for validation before schedule is enabled in prod
Soft-delete window of 7 days with automatic notifications and rollback tooling during initial rollout
Canary rollout by tenant size: small tenants first, then medium, then large
Manual kill-switch exposed in Console and via API for emergency pause
